questions.note: Order reads right (hallux longest, toe 2 a little shorter, 3-5 descending) and knuckles and pulps exist, but toes 2-5 are smooth plump tubes with almost no wrinkles or redness over the joints (hr.lesser, V5f); from below they are ringed like caterpillars with pinched silhouettes; toe 5 lies beside toe 4 instead of under it.

Ten plates with free-edge thickness and none floating or sunk, but every nail carries the same bright white French-tip strip on a flat, opaque pale-pink plate; the lesser nails are one rounded tombstone scaled down; the hallux plate is a glossy acrylic tile with a white crescent at its base, no lateral folds over it and no pink bed or soft lunula.

Veins now exist as relief (they bump the silhouette in V1f and V3) and the saphenous passes in front of the medial malleolus, but every vessel is a thin, even cord paler than the skin, like silicone string or scars, and the dorsum is laced with a web of them. The tendons are evenly spaced ridges of equal strength to every web; the EHL does not lead.

Toe shadow sides stay dark and the toes do not glow, but dorsum, toes and heel are one smooth, unzoned peach like silicone, with hardly any cells or pits in V5f, while the pads carry a crisp procedural ridge field (corduroy, target whorls with straight seams). The heel callus is a crackle-glaze mesh and the medial malleolus glows (V1f).

defects.what: The great saphenous and the medial dorsal loop are thin, even-width cords paler than the skin with a white core, like silicone string under the surface; the loop on the medial dorsum is a closed U of constant width.
defects.fix: Real superficial veins are soft 3 mm cords a touch darker and bluer-green than the skin, tapering, branching and fading into the tissue, lit only on the crest; drop the pale albedo along the vein mask.

defects.what: The dorsum is laced with a dense web of thin pale lines (the arch, its tributaries and a line to every web) of one width and tone, which reads as scars or crackle rather than veins at native size.
defects.fix: One arch with a few fat tributaries and plain skin between them; vessels low, soft-edged, 2.5-3 mm wide, slightly darker than the skin, and fewer.

defects.what: The instep and metatarsal dorsum carry no hair in any view, so the foot looks shaved; the spec requires 90-160 terminal hairs there and only a few dashes sit on the toe bases.
defects.fix: Sparse dark terminal hairs, 6-10 mm, lying flat toward the toes over the distal dorsum and thinning toward ankle and toes, as in the anchor photos.

defects.what: At native size all five nails carry the same thin bright-white free-edge strip on a flat, opaque pale-pink plate, a French pedicure; the same white tips show at every toe in V1f and V3.
defects.fix: Toenail free edges are thin, translucent, off-white to yellowish and uneven, often with grey grime beneath; the plate shows the pink bed fading toward the edge, not one pastel.

defects.what: The hallux plate sits on the toe like a glued acrylic tile: one even glossy pale pink, a crisp outline with no lateral folds over it, a bright white crescent at its base like a lifted edge, and a clean uniform cream free edge.
defects.fix: A real toenail tucks under a soft cuticle and lateral folds, shows a pink bed, a paler onychodermal band, a soft milky lunula, faint yellowing and ridges, and some grime under the edge.

defects.what: Nails 2-5 are one rounded tombstone shape scaled down, each with the same white edge line and pale pink fill; nothing changes from toe to toe.
defects.fix: Lesser toenails are narrower, more curved and irregular, the 4th short, the 5th small, thickened, ridged and partly buried in its fold, each with its own tint.

defects.what: Toes 3-5 are smooth plump tubes: soft knuckle bumps with no transverse wrinkles over the PIP or DIP, no redness, and smooth skin right up to the nail folds.
defects.fix: Real lesser toes show 3-6 creases over each knuckle, redder and rougher skin there, a small corn on toe 4, and drier, lined skin around the nail folds.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are five evenly spaced parallel ridges of equal height running at full strength to every web, like piano keys; the EHL is no stronger than the slips to toes 2-5.
defects.fix: With the toes relaxed the EHL is the one clear cord; the EDL slips are faint, converge toward the ankle and fade into the MTP knuckles before the webs.

defects.what: From behind, the Achilles is one hard vertical crease with a glossy streak along it and a flat plane beside it, so there is no rounded cord narrowing into the heel and no hollow on either side.
defects.fix: The tendon is a rounded 16 mm cord, narrowest a few cm above the heel, flanked by soft hollows on both sides, with a soft sheen rather than a streak.

defects.what: The medial malleolus is a round ball under the skin with a soft glowing hotspot and no firm light-to-shadow turn; in V2 it sits over a dark pocket, like a sphere pushed under a sheet.
defects.fix: The medial malleolus is a broad, flat-faced bony prominence continuous with the tibia, with a firm edge, a crisper terminator and only a shallow groove below it.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a soft, padded, low-contrast swelling, not a pointed bony knob with hollows in front of and behind it.
defects.fix: The fibula's tip is a sharper, lower, more posterior knob with a clear hollow in front (sinus tarsi) and behind (peroneal groove).

defects.what: From the medial side the foot is nearly flat: the medial border hangs only a few mm above the floor from heel to ball and the instep is a straight ramp.
defects.fix: A fit man's medial arch lifts clearly off the floor between heel and ball, and the instep domes over the navicular and medial cuneiform.

defects.what: Only the heel carries callus: the ball under the 1st-2nd metatarsal heads is pink and smooth, and the lateral 5th MTP and the medial hallux IP show no pale rough skin, so the foot reads unworn.
defects.fix: A boot-wearing soldier has pale, yellowish, rougher skin with soft edges under the 1st-2nd MT heads, on the lateral 5th MTP and on the medial hallux IP.

defects.what: The heel callus is an even mesh of thin dark polygons on grey-cream, like crackle glaze, under a fringe of white salt speckle where its mask fades out.
defects.fix: Heel callus is a thick yellowish rim with a few deeper fissures running up from the edge, flaky at their lips, blending into normal skin over several mm.

defects.what: The ball and toe bases carry one unbroken field of parallel wavy ridges of the same pitch, depth and direction everywhere, like corduroy.
defects.fix: Plantar ridges turn with the ball and around the toe bases, break at creases, flatten under callus, and at this scale show mainly under grazing light.

defects.what: The hallux pad's whorl is a perfect target of concentric ovals with a straight seam from the IP crease into its core where the ridge phase jumps; no endings, forks or pores. Toes 2 and 3 carry the same target.
defects.fix: A real pad's whorl or loop is irregular, with ridge endings, bifurcations, pores along the ridges and a triradius, and no seam.

defects.what: From below, the lesser toes are ringed with deep, even creases that pinch their silhouettes into stacked segments, like caterpillars (also V4).
defects.fix: Plantar toe creases are shallow folds between fleshy pads that bulge sideways; the outline stays smooth.

defects.what: Toe 5 lies beside toe 4 as a separate small toe at the same level, its nail facing the camera, instead of rolling outward and tucking partly under toe 4.
defects.fix: The fifth toe rolls 35-40 degrees and tucks under the 4th, its nail facing up and out, part of it hidden beneath toe 4.

defects.what: The lateral border runs smooth through mid-foot with no 5th metatarsal styloid bump; the only lump on it is a vein ridge well behind where the styloid belongs.
defects.fix: The 5th metatarsal base makes a sharp bump about halfway along the lateral border, a little above the sole.

defects.what: The toe hairs are dead-straight, untapered dark dashes standing parallel to each other like pen strokes on the skin; the hallux tuft is the same parallel hatching (V1f zoom).
defects.fix: Real toe hairs are fine, tapered and gently curved, lie on the skin toward the tips at varied angles and cast a faint shadow.

defects.what: Toe 3 is crossed by a ruler-straight hairline with a tone step and a notch where it meets the silhouette, and toe 4 has a similar line at its base: a seam, not a flexion crease.
defects.fix: A flexion crease is a soft, slightly curved fold, deepest mid-toe and fading at the sides, with no tone change across it.

ranked: [D1] The veins are the loudest tell: the great saphenous and the medial loop (V2) are thin, even, paler-than-skin cords with a white core, like silicone string glued under the skin. Real veins are soft cords a touch darker and bluer-green than the skin that taper and fade.

[D2] Across the dorsum (V1f, V3) the arch, its tributaries and a line to every web make a dense web of thin pale lines of one width, reading as scars or crackle; a real dorsum shows one arch and a few fat vessels on plain skin.

The skin is too smooth, clean and even: one unzoned peach over dorsum, toes and heel, almost no cells or pits in V5f, no redder knuckles or tips; with the nails it reads as a young pedicured silicone foot, not a 40-year-old soldier's.
[D3] The dorsum is bare in every view, so the foot looks shaved; men's feet, as in the anchor, carry sparse dark hair over the distal dorsum and a tuft on the big toe.
[D4] At native size every nail carries the same bright white free-edge strip on a flat pale-pink plate, a French pedicure; the white tips show even in V1f and V3.

[D5] The hallux plate is a glossy acrylic tile: even pale pink, a crisp outline with no lateral folds over it, a white crescent at its base like a lifted edge, and a clean cream free edge with no grime under it.
[D6] Nails 2-5 are one rounded tombstone scaled down, same fill and same white line; real lesser toenails differ toe to toe, the 5th small, thick and half-buried in its fold.
[D7] Toes 2-5 are smooth plump tubes: knuckle bumps without wrinkles or redness, smooth skin up to the nail folds, round glossy pulps.
[D8] The extensor tendons are evenly spaced parallel ridges of equal height running to every web, like piano keys (V5f); with the toes relaxed the EHL leads and the EDL slips fade before the webs.
[D9] From behind (V8) the Achilles is a single hard crease with a glossy streak and a flat plane beside it, so no rounded cord narrows into the heel between two hollows.
[D10] The medial malleolus is a ball with a soft glowing hotspot (V1f) over a dark pocket (V2), like a sphere under a sheet; the real one is a broad, flat-faced bony prominence with a firmer edge.
[D11] The lateral malleolus is a soft padded swelling (V3); the outside of the ankle lacks the sharp lower knob and the hollows in front of and behind it.
[D12] The medial arch barely lifts off the floor and the instep is a straight ramp (V2): the flat generic base-mesh foot rather than a fit man's arched one.
[D13] Only the heel has callus; the ball is pink and smooth and the 5th MTP and hallux IP are clean (V4), so the foot reads unworn rather than boot-worn.

[D14] The heel callus (V8) is an even mesh of fine dark polygons like crackle glaze under a fringe of white salt speckle where its mask fades; real heel callus has a few deep fissures and a soft edge.
Detail is uneven: in hr.plantar the sole and pads carry crisp, high-contrast ridges while the dorsum, toes and heel elsewhere are nearly featureless, so the ridges read as applied rather than grown.
[D15] The ball and toe bases are one unbroken corduroy of parallel wavy ridges of the same pitch, depth and direction everywhere (hr.plantar).
[D16] Each pad's whorl is a perfect target of concentric ovals; the hallux and toe 3 have a straight seam into the core where the ridges jump, and no pad has ridge endings, forks or pores.
[D17] From below (V4, hr.plantar) the lesser toes are stacked rings whose deep creases pinch the silhouette, like caterpillars, rather than fleshy pads.
[D18] Toe 5 lies beside toe 4 at the same level (V5f) instead of rolling outward and tucking partly under it.
[D19] The lateral border runs smooth through mid-foot with no 5th metatarsal styloid; the only bump is a vein ridge further back (V3).
[D20] The few toe hairs are straight, untapered, parallel dark dashes like pen strokes, and the hallux tuft is the same hatching (V1f zoom).
[D21] Toe 3's plantar crease is a ruler-straight hairline with a tone step and a notch at the edge, and toe 4 has one at its base: seams, not folds.
